highlights.title: Google’s new AI boss inherits a race to catch OpenAI and Anthropic
highlights.description: Koray Kavukcuoglu is taking charge of Google DeepMind as it tries to keep Gemini competitive with OpenAI and Anthropic.

highlights.title: Z.ai to Rival Anthropic, OpenAI in Coding With New AI Model
highlights.description: Z.ai Co. is set to upgrade its flagship AI model, adding to a series of Chinese open-weight offerings seeking to outcompete Anthropic PBC and OpenAI.

highlights.title: AI Safety Fears Grow After Multiple Breaches
highlights.description: The infiltration of Hugging Face by OpenAI's agents has put AI-enabled cyber attacks into the spotlight. The incident and similar breaches reported by Anthropic PBC and Meta Platforms Inc. have fueled calls in Washington and Silicon Valley for more thorough safety reviews of artificial intelligence models. Bloomberg's Jordan Robertson reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

highlights.title: Anthropic Said in Talks to Buy Startup Decart for $6 Billion
highlights.description: Anthropic PBC is in talks to buy the artificial intelligence startup Decart AI for about $6 billion, according to people familiar with the matter.

highlights.description: Alibaba Group Holding Ltd., Baidu Inc. and Kuaishou Technology are the next big names in tech that will have to address concerns over the mounting financial costs needed to sustain intense AI competition.

highlights.title: Uber partners with China's Pony.ai for 2,000 robotaxis in Europe
highlights.description: The rollout comes as robotaxi fleet sizes become increasingly critical for commercialization.

highlights.title: Kushner’s Thrive Fund Grows Sevenfold to $3.7 Billion on AI Bets
highlights.description: Thrive Capital’s 2022 early-stage venture capital fund, a $516 million investment vehicle that made early bets on OpenAI, SpaceX and Anduril Industries Inc., has grown to be worth more than $3.7 billion as of the end of June.

highlights.description: Meta Platforms Inc. says it has removed access to more than 750,000 Instagram and Facebook accounts in Australia believed to belong to people under 16 since it began complying with the country’s landmark youth social media ban last year.

It’s currently not clear if this new initiative is intended to be permanent, or a limited time promotion. The service experimented with something similar a few years ago, but it didn’t last too long.
